raw: CHAPTER IX. The Gorgon’s Head
en: [Chapter 9] The Gorgon’s Head

raw: It was a heavy mass of building, that chateau of Monsieur the Marquis, with a large stone courtyard before it, and two stone sweeps of staircase meeting in a stone terrace before the principal door.
en: The Marquis’s castle was a heavy stone building, with a large stone courtyard in front, and two curved stone staircases meeting at a stone terrace before the main entrance. It was a stony place altogether.
ko: 후작의 성은 무거운 돌로 된 건물이었고, 앞에는 커다란 돌 마당이 있었으며, 주 출입구 앞의 돌 테라스에서 만나는 구부러진 두 개의 돌계단이 있었다. 그곳은 온통 돌로 된 장소였다.

raw: A stony business altogether, with heavy stone balustrades, and stone urns, and stone flowers, and stone faces of men, and stone heads of lions, in all directions.
en: Heavy stone balustrades lined every edge. Stone urns and stone flowers stood at every turn. And stone faces, men and lions alike, stared out in every direction.
ko: 무거운 돌 난간들이 모든 가장자리를 따라 늘어서 있었다. 구석마다 돌로 된 항아리와 돌로 된 꽃들이 서 있었다. 그리고 사람과 사자 할 것 없이 돌로 된 얼굴들이 사방을 노려보고 있었다.

raw: As if the Gorgon’s head had surveyed it, when it was finished, two centuries ago.
en: It looked as if the mythical Gorgon’s head had looked at it when it was finished two hundred years ago, turning the whole place to stone.
ko: 마치 이백 년 전 그것이 완공되었을 때 신화 속 고르곤의 머리가 그것을 쳐다보아, 그곳 전체를 돌로 만들어버린 것 같았다.

raw: Up the broad flight of shallow steps, Monsieur the Marquis, flambeau preceded, went from his carriage, sufficiently disturbing the darkness to elicit loud remonstrance from an owl in the roof of the great pile of stable building away among the trees.
en: Up the broad, shallow steps walked the Marquis, preceded by a servant carrying a torch. His arrival disturbed the darkness enough to make an owl in the stable roof hoot loudly.
ko: 횃불을 든 하인을 앞세우고, 후작은 넓고 얕은 계단을 걸어 올라갔다. 그의 도착은 마구간 지붕의 부엉이가 크게 울어댈 만큼 어둠을 방해했다.

raw: All else was so quiet, that the flambeau carried up the steps, and the other flambeau held at the great door, burnt as if they were in a close room of state, instead of being in the open night-air.
en: Everything else was so quiet that the torch carried up the steps and another held at the entrance burned steadily, as if they were in a closed room rather than the open night air.
ko: 다른 모든 것들은 너무나 조용해서, 계단 위로 들고 올라간 횃불과 입구에서 들고 있는 또 다른 횃불은 마치 열린 밤공기 속이 아니라 닫힌 방 안에 있는 것처럼 흔들림 없이 타올랐다.

raw: Other sound than the owl’s voice there was none, save the falling of a fountain into its stone basin; for, it was one of those dark nights that hold their breath by the hour together, and then heave a long low sigh, and hold their breath again.
en: The only sounds were the owl's hooting and the splashing of the fountain into its stone basin. It was one of those dark nights that seem to hold their breath for hours, sighing softly before holding their breath again.
ko: 유일한 소리는 부엉이의 울음소리와 분수대에서 돌 물받이로 떨어지는 물소리뿐이었다. 그것은 몇 시간 동안 숨을 참았다가 부드럽게 한숨을 쉬고는 다시 숨을 참는 듯한, 그런 어두운 밤 중 하나였다.

raw: The great door clanged behind him, and Monsieur the Marquis crossed a hall grim with certain old boar-spears, swords, and knives of the chase; grimmer with certain heavy riding-rods and riding-whips, of which many a peasant, gone to his benefactor Death, had felt the weight when his lord was angry.
en: The great door slammed shut behind him. The Marquis walked through a hall decorated with old boar spears, swords, and hunting knives. It was made even grimmer by the heavy riding whips on the walls, many of which had been felt by the local peasants when their lord was angry.
ko: 거대한 문이 그의 등 뒤로 쾅 닫혔다. 후작은 낡은 멧돼지 창과 칼, 사냥용 칼로 장식된 넓은 방을 걸어 지나갔다. 벽에 걸린 무거운 승마용 채찍들 때문에 그곳은 더욱 음울해 보였는데, 영주가 화를 낼 때면 그 채찍들 중 상당수를 지역 농부들이 몸소 느꼈다.

raw: Avoiding the larger rooms, which were dark and made fast for the night, Monsieur the Marquis, with his flambeau-bearer going on before, went up the staircase to a door in a corridor.
en: Avoiding the larger rooms, which were dark and locked for the night, the Marquis followed his torchbearer upstairs to a room in the corridor.
ko: 어둡고 밤을 위해 잠겨 있는 큰 방들을 피해, 후작은 횃불잡이를 따라 위층 복도에 있는 한 방으로 갔다.

raw: This thrown open, admitted him to his own private apartment of three rooms: his bed-chamber and two others.
en: This door opened into his private suite of three rooms: his bedroom and two others.
ko: 이 문은 그의 개인 공간인 세 개의 방, 즉 침실과 다른 두 방으로 이어졌다.

raw: High vaulted rooms with cool uncarpeted floors, great dogs upon the hearths for the burning of wood in winter time, and all luxuries befitting the state of a marquis in a luxurious age and country.
en: They were high-ceilinged, vaulted rooms with cool uncarpeted floors, massive iron dogs in the fireplaces for burning wood in the winter, and every luxury suited to the lifestyle of a marquis in a wealthy age and country.
ko: 그곳은 카펫이 깔리지 않은 서늘한 바닥, 겨울에 장작을 태우기 위해 벽난로에 놓인 거대한 무쇠 개 장식, 부유한 시대와 나라의 후작이라는 생활 방식에 걸맞은 모든 사치품을 갖춘 천장이 높고 둥근 방들이었다.

raw: The fashion of the last Louis but one, of the line that was never to break--the fourteenth Louis--was conspicuous in their rich furniture; but, it was diversified by many objects that were illustrations of old pages in the history of France.
en: They were filled with luxuries suitable for a nobleman of that wealthy era. The style of King Louis XIV was visible in the rich furniture, alongside decorations showing older pages of French history.
ko: 그곳은 그 부유한 시대의 귀족에게 어울리는 사치품들로 가득했다. 화려한 가구들에는 루이 14세의 양식이 보였고, 프랑스 역사의 더 오래된 페이지들을 보여주는 장식들도 함께 있었다.

raw: A supper-table was laid for two, in the third of the rooms; a round room, in one of the chateau’s four extinguisher-topped towers.
en: A dinner table was set for two in the third room, which was a round room located in one of the castle's towers.
ko: 세 번째 방에는 두 사람을 위한 저녁 식탁이 차려져 있었는데, 그곳은 성의 탑 중 하나에 위치한 둥근 방이었다.

raw: A small lofty room, with its window wide open, and the wooden jalousie-blinds closed, so that the dark night only showed in slight horizontal lines of black, alternating with their broad lines of stone colour.
en: It was a small, high room with its window wide open and the wooden blinds closed, so the dark night showed only as thin black lines between the blinds.
ko: 그곳은 작고 높은 방으로, 창문은 활짝 열려 있고 나무 블라인드는 닫혀 있어서, 어두운 밤이 블라인드 사이의 가느다란 검은 선으로만 보였다.

raw: “My nephew,” said the Marquis, glancing at the supper preparation; “they said he was not arrived.”
en: "My nephew," said the Marquis, looking at the table. "They said he had not arrived."
ko: "내 조카," 식탁을 바라보며 후작이 말했다. "아직 도착하지 않았다고 하더군."

raw: Nor was he; but, he had been expected with Monseigneur.
en: He had not, but he had been expected to arrive with the Marquis.
ko: 그는 도착하지 않았지만, 후작과 함께 도착할 것으로 예상되었다.

raw: “Ah!
en: "Ah!

raw: It is not probable he will arrive to-night; nevertheless, leave the table as it is.
en: He probably won't arrive tonight, but leave the table as it is.
ko: 그는 아마 오늘 밤에는 오지 않을 테지만, 식탁은 그대로 두어라.

raw: I shall be ready in a quarter of an hour.”
en: I will be ready in fifteen minutes."
ko: 십오 분 후에 준비를 마치겠다."

raw: In a quarter of an hour Monseigneur was ready, and sat down alone to his sumptuous and choice supper.
en: Fifteen minutes later, the Marquis sat down alone to his dinner. His chair faced the window.
ko: 십오 분 후, 후작은 혼자 앉아 저녁 식사를 했다. 그의 의자는 창문을 향해 있었다.

raw: His chair was opposite to the window, and he had taken his soup, and was raising his glass of Bordeaux to his lips, when he put it down.
en: He had finished his soup and was raising his glass of Bordeaux wine to his lips when he suddenly put it down.
ko: 그가 수프를 다 먹고 보르도 와인 잔을 입술로 가져가던 중 갑자기 그것을 내려놓았다.

raw: “What is that?” he calmly asked, looking with attention at the horizontal lines of black and stone colour.
en: "What is that?" he asked calmly, looking at the blinds.
ko: "저게 무엇이냐?" 블라인드를 바라보며 그가 침착하게 물었다.

raw: “Monseigneur?
en: "Monseigneur?
ko: "영주님?

raw: That?”
en: What?"
ko: 무엇을 말씀이십니까?"

raw: “Outside the blinds.
en: "Outside the blinds.
ko: "블라인드 바깥 말이다.

raw: Open the blinds.”
en: Open them."
ko: 열어라."

raw: It was done.
en: The servant did so.
ko: 하인이 그렇게 했다.

raw: “Well?”
en: "Well?"
ko: "그래서?"

raw: “Monseigneur, it is nothing.
en: "Monseigneur, there is nothing.
ko: "영주님, 아무것도 없습니다.

raw: The trees and the night are all that are here.”
en: Just the trees and the night."
ko: 그저 나무들과 밤뿐입니다."

raw: The servant who spoke, had thrown the blinds wide, had looked out into the vacant darkness, and stood with that blank behind him, looking round for instructions.
en: The servant had opened the blinds and looked out into the darkness, then stood waiting for instructions.
ko: 하인은 블라인드를 열고 어둠 속을 내다본 다음, 지시를 기다리며 서 있었다.

raw: “Good,” said the imperturbable master. “Close them again.”
en: "Good," said the calm master. "Close them again."
ko: "좋다," 침착한 주인이 말했다. "다시 닫아라."

raw: That was done too, and the Marquis went on with his supper.
en: This was done, and the Marquis went on eating.
ko: 이 일이 처리되었고, 후작은 계속해서 식사를 했다.

raw: He was half way through it, when he again stopped with his glass in his hand, hearing the sound of wheels.
en: He was halfway through his meal when he stopped again, glass in hand, hearing the sound of wheels.
ko: 식사를 반쯤 마쳤을 때 그는 바퀴 소리를 듣고 한 손에 잔을 든 채 다시 멈칫했다.

raw: It came on briskly, and came up to the front of the chateau.
en: A carriage drove up quickly to the front of the castle.
ko: 마차 한 대가 성 앞쪽으로 빠르게 달려왔다.

raw: “Ask who is arrived.”
en: "Find out who has arrived."
ko: "누가 도착했는지 알아보아라."

raw: It was the nephew of Monseigneur.
en: It was the Marquis's nephew.
ko: 그는 후작의 조카였다.

raw: He had been some few leagues behind Monseigneur, early in the afternoon. He had diminished the distance rapidly, but not so rapidly as to come up with Monseigneur on the road.
en: He had been traveling behind his uncle earlier in the afternoon, closing the distance but not catching up on the road.
ko: 그는 오후 일찍부터 삼촌의 뒤를 따라 여행하고 있었는데, 거리를 좁히긴 했지만 길에서 따라잡지는 못했다.

raw: He had heard of Monseigneur, at the posting-houses, as being before him.
en: At the post houses, they had told him his uncle was ahead of him.
ko: 역참에서 사람들은 삼촌이 그보다 앞서가고 있다고 그에게 말해주었다.

raw: He was to be told (said Monseigneur) that supper awaited him then and there, and that he was prayed to come to it.
en: He was told that dinner was waiting for him, and he was asked to join.
ko: 그는 저녁 식사가 그를 위해 준비되어 있다는 말을 들었고, 함께 식사하자는 요청을 받았다.

raw: In a little while he came.
en: Soon he entered.
ko: 곧 그가 들어왔다.

raw: He had been known in England as Charles Darnay.
en: In England, he was known as Charles Darnay.
ko: 영국에서 그는 찰스 다네이로 알려져 있었다.

raw: Monseigneur received him in a courtly manner, but they did not shake hands.
en: The Marquis received him politely, but they did not shake hands.
ko: 후작은 그를 정중하게 맞이했지만, 그들은 악수를 하지는 않았다.

raw: “You left Paris yesterday, sir?” he said to Monseigneur, as he took his seat at table.
en: "You left Paris yesterday, sir?" Darnay asked as he sat down.
ko: "어제 파리를 떠나셨습니까, 삼촌?" 다네이가 자리에 앉으며 물었다.

raw: “Yesterday.
en: "Yesterday.
ko: "어제 떠났다.

raw: And you?”
en: And you?"
ko: 너는?"

raw: “I come direct.”
en: "I came straight here."
ko: "저는 바로 이리로 왔습니다."

raw: “From London?”
en: "From London?"
ko: "런던에서?"

raw: “Yes.”
en: "Yes."

raw: “You have been a long time coming,” said the Marquis, with a smile.
en: "You took a long time to make the journey," the Marquis said with a smile.
ko: "여행에 시간이 꽤 걸렸구나," 후작이 미소를 지으며 말했다.

raw: “On the contrary; I come direct.”
en: "On the contrary, I came directly."
ko: "오히려 저는 곧장 왔습니다."

raw: “Pardon me!
en: "Excuse me!
ko: "미안하구나!

raw: I mean, not a long time on the journey; a long time intending the journey.”
en: I don't mean the journey took long; I mean it took you a long time to decide to come."
ko: 여행이 오래 걸렸다는 뜻이 아니라, 네가 오기로 결정하는 데 오랜 시간이 걸렸다는 뜻이다."

raw: “I have been detained by”--the nephew stopped a moment in his answer--“various business.”
en: "I was delayed by various business," the nephew replied.
ko: "여러 가지 일들로 늦어졌습니다," 조카가 대답했다.

raw: “Without doubt,” said the polished uncle.
en: "No doubt," said the polite uncle.
ko: "틀림없겠지," 정중한 삼촌이 말했다.

raw: So long as a servant was present, no other words passed between them.
en: As long as the servant was in the room, they said nothing else.
ko: 하인이 방에 있는 동안, 그들은 더 이상 아무 말도 하지 않았다.

raw: When coffee had been served and they were alone together, the nephew, looking at the uncle and meeting the eyes of the face that was like a fine mask, opened a conversation.
en: Once coffee was served and they were alone, the nephew looked at his uncle's mask-like face and began to speak.
ko: 커피가 나오고 그들만 남게 되자, 조카는 삼촌의 가면 같은 얼굴을 쳐다보며 말하기 시작했다.

raw: “I have come back, sir, as you anticipate, pursuing the object that took me away.
en: "I have returned, sir, to finish the business that took me away.
ko: "저는 저를 떠나게 했던 일을 끝내기 위해 돌아왔습니다, 삼촌.

raw: It carried me into great and unexpected peril; but it is a sacred object, and if it had carried me to death I hope it would have sustained me.”
en: It led me into great and unexpected danger, but it is a sacred duty. Even if it had led to my death, I hope it would have supported me."
ko: 그 일은 저를 크고 예상치 못한 위험으로 이끌었지만, 그것은 신성한 의무입니다. 비록 그것이 저를 죽음으로 이끌었더라도, 저는 그것이 저를 지탱해주었기를 바랍니다."

raw: “Not to death,” said the uncle; “it is not necessary to say, to death.”
en: "Not to death," the uncle said. "There is no need to say that."
ko: "죽음까지는 아니지," 삼촌이 말했다. "그렇게까지 말할 필요는 없다."

raw: “I doubt, sir,” returned the nephew, “whether, if it had carried me to the utmost brink of death, you would have cared to stop me there.”
en: The nephew replied, "I doubt, sir, that if I had been on the brink of death, you would have done anything to save me." He said it plainly, without rage, just as a man states a fact he has long known to be true.
ko: 조카는 대답했다, "제가 죽음의 문턱에 있었더라도, 삼촌이 저를 구하기 위해 어떤 일이든 하셨을지 의문입니다." 그는 오랫동안 진실로 알고 있던 사실을 말하는 사람처럼 분노 없이 담담하게 말했다.

raw: The deepened marks in the nose, and the lengthening of the fine straight lines in the cruel face, looked ominous as to that; the uncle made a graceful gesture of protest, which was so clearly a slight form of good breeding that it was not reassuring.
en: The pinched nostrils and the sharp lines on the uncle's face tightened ominously. He made a polite gesture of protest, but it was purely a social formality and not reassuring.
ko: 삼촌의 얼굴에 있는 오뚝한 콧방울과 날카로운 선들이 불길하게 일그러졌다. 그는 정중하게 항의하는 제스처를 취했지만, 그것은 순전히 사교적인 형식이었고 전혀 안심이 되지 않았다.

raw: “Indeed, sir,” pursued the nephew, “for anything I know, you may have expressly worked to give a more suspicious appearance to the suspicious circumstances that surrounded me.”
en: The nephew continued, "Indeed, sir, for all I know, you may have helped make the suspicious circumstances around me look even worse." He did not raise his voice. He simply kept going.
ko: 조카는 계속했다, "사실상, 제가 아는 한 삼촌은 제 주위의 의심스러운 상황들을 훨씬 더 나쁘게 보이도록 도왔을지도 모릅니다." 그는 목소리를 높이지 않았다. 그저 계속 말을 이어갔다.

raw: “No, no, no,” said the uncle, pleasantly.
en: "No, no, no," the uncle said pleasantly.
ko: "아니다, 아니야," 삼촌은 유쾌하게 말했다.

raw: “But, however that may be,” resumed the nephew, glancing at him with deep distrust, “I know that your diplomacy would stop me by any means, and would know no scruple as to means.”
en: The nephew said, "However that may be, I know you would stop me by any means, and would have no moral objections to those means." He looked at his uncle with deep distrust as he said it.
ko: 조카는 말했다, "어찌 됐든 간에, 삼촌이 어떤 수단을 써서라도 저를 막으려 할 것이고, 그 수단에 대해 어떤 도덕적 거리낌도 가지지 않을 거란 걸 저는 압니다." 그는 깊은 불신을 담아 삼촌을 바라보며 말했다.

raw: “My friend, I told you so,” said the uncle, with a fine pulsation in the two marks. “Do me the favour to recall that I told you so, long ago.”
en: "My friend, I told you so," said the uncle, his nostrils twitching. "Please remember that I told you so long ago."
ko: "내 친구여, 내가 그렇게 말하지 않았느냐," 콧방울을 씰룩거리며 삼촌이 말했다. "내가 오래전에 그렇게 말했던 것을 부디 기억해 주렴."

raw: “I recall it.”
en: "I remember."
ko: "기억합니다."

raw: “Thank you,” said the Marquis--very sweetly indeed.
en: "Thank you," the Marquis said sweetly.
ko: "고맙구나," 후작이 다정하게 말했다.

raw: His tone lingered in the air, almost like the tone of a musical instrument.
en: His polite tone lingered in the air like a musical note.
ko: 그의 정중한 어조가 마치 음표처럼 공기 중에 맴돌았다.

raw: “In effect, sir,” pursued the nephew, “I believe it to be at once your bad fortune, and my good fortune, that has kept me out of a prison in France here.”
en: The nephew continued, "In fact, sir, I believe it is both your misfortune and my good luck that I am not in a French prison right now."
ko: 조카가 계속했다, "사실, 삼촌, 제가 지금 프랑스 감옥에 있지 않은 것은 삼촌의 불운이자 저의 행운이라고 생각합니다."

raw: “I do not quite understand,” returned the uncle, sipping his coffee. “Dare I ask you to explain?”
en: "I don't quite understand," the uncle said, sipping his coffee. "Would you explain?"
ko: "잘 이해가 안 되는구나," 삼촌이 커피를 홀짝이며 말했다. "설명해 주겠니?"

raw: “I believe that if you were not in disgrace with the Court, and had not been overshadowed by that cloud for years past, a letter de cachet would have sent me to some fortress indefinitely.”
en: "I believe that if you were not in disgrace with the royal court, you would have used a secret arrest warrant to throw me into a fortress indefinitely."
ko: "저는 삼촌이 왕실에서 신임을 잃은 상태가 아니었다면, 비밀 체포 영장을 사용해 저를 요새 감옥에 무기한 가둬두셨을 거라고 믿습니다."

raw: “It is possible,” said the uncle, with great calmness. “For the honour of the family, I could even resolve to incommode you to that extent.
en: "It is possible," the uncle said calmly. "For the honor of the family, I would gladly lock you up.
ko: "가능한 일이지," 삼촌이 차분하게 말했다. "가문의 명예를 위해서라면 나는 기꺼이 너를 가두었을 거다.

raw: Pray excuse me!”
en: Please excuse me!"
ko: 부디 용서하거라!"

raw: “I perceive that, happily for me, the Reception of the day before yesterday was, as usual, a cold one,” observed the nephew.
en: "I see that, fortunately for me, your reception at court the day before yesterday was cold as usual," the nephew remarked.
ko: "다행히도, 엊그제 궁정에서의 삼촌에 대한 대우가 평소처럼 차가웠던 것으로 보 গঠন입니다," 조카가 언급했다.

raw: “I would not say happily, my friend,” returned the uncle, with refined politeness; “I would not be sure of that.
en: "I wouldn't say fortunately, my friend," the uncle replied politely.
ko: "다행이라고는 할 수 없지, 내 친구여," 삼촌이 정중하게 대답했다.

raw: A good opportunity for consideration, surrounded by the advantages of solitude, might influence your destiny to far greater advantage than you influence it for yourself.
en: "A period of quiet reflection in prison might help you more than you help yourself.
ko: "감옥에서의 조용한 반성의 시간이 네가 네 자신을 돕는 것보다 더 도움이 될지도 모른다.

raw: But it is useless to discuss the question.
en: But there is no point in discussing it.
ko: 하지만 그것에 대해 논의하는 것은 의미가 없지.

raw: I am, as you say, at a disadvantage.
en: As you say, I am at a disadvantage now.
ko: 네 말대로, 나는 지금 불리한 입장에 있다.

raw: These little instruments of correction, these gentle aids to the power and honour of families, these slight favours that might so incommode you, are only to be obtained now by interest and importunity.
en: Those little warrants of punishment, those gentle aids to a family's power and honor, those slight favors that would trouble you so much, can only be obtained now through influence and persistent begging.
ko: 그런 작은 처벌 영장들, 가문의 권력과 명예에 대한 부드러운 지원들, 너를 그토록 괴롭힐 수 있는 그런 사소한 호의들은 이제 영향력과 끊임없는 간청을 통해서만 얻을 수 있단다.

raw: They are sought by so many, and they are granted (comparatively) to so few!
en: It didn't use to be this way, but France has changed for the worse.
ko: 예전에는 이러지 않았지만, 프랑스가 나쁜 쪽으로 변했구나.

raw: It used not to be so, but France in all such things is changed for the worse.
en: Our ancestors held the power of life and death over the peasants.
ko: 우리 조상들은 소작농들에 대한 생사여탈권을 쥐고 있었다.

raw: Our not remote ancestors held the right of life and death over the surrounding vulgar.
en: From this very room, many peasants have been taken out to be hanged.
ko: 바로 이 방에서 수많은 소작농들이 끌려나가 교수형을 당했지.

raw: From this room, many such dogs have been taken out to be hanged; in the next room (my bedroom), one fellow, to our knowledge, was poniarded on the spot for professing some insolent delicacy respecting his daughter--_his_ daughter?
en: In the next room, my bedroom, a man was stabbed to death for protesting when we took his daughter. We have lost many privileges.
ko: 옆 방, 내 침실에서는 우리가 그의 딸을 데려간 것에 항의하던 한 남자가 칼에 찔려 죽었다. 우리는 많은 특권을 잃었어.

raw: We have lost many privileges; a new philosophy has become the mode; and the assertion of our station, in these days, might (I do not go so far as to say would, but might) cause us real inconvenience.
en: We have lost many privileges; a new philosophy has become fashionable; and asserting our high position these days might—I won't go so far as to say would, but might—cause us real inconvenience.
ko: 우리는 많은 특권을 잃었다. 새로운 철학이 유행하게 되었고, 요즘 우리의 높은 지위를 주장하는 것은—그럴 것이라고까지는 말하지 않겠지만—우리에게 진짜 불편을 초래할지도 모른다.

raw: All very bad, very bad!”
en: It is all very bad!"
ko: 모든 것이 아주 나빠졌어!"

raw: The Marquis took a gentle little pinch of snuff, and shook his head; as elegantly despondent as he could becomingly be of a country still containing himself, that great means of regeneration.
en: The Marquis took a pinch of snuff and shook his head, looking elegantly sad about a country that still had him to guide it.
ko: 후작은 코담배를 한 줌 쥐고 고개를 저으며, 여전히 그를 지도자로 둔 나라에 대해 우아하고 슬픈 표정을 지었다.

raw: “We have so asserted our station, both in the old time and in the modern time also,” said the nephew, gloomily, “that I believe our name to be more detested than any name in France.”
en: The nephew said gloomily, "We have asserted our high position so much, both in the past and now, that I believe our family name is detested more than any other in France."
ko: 조카가 우울하게 말했다, "우리는 과거나 지금이나 우리의 높은 지위를 너무 많이 주장해왔기 때문에, 저는 우리 가문의 이름이 프랑스의 어떤 이름보다 더 혐오의 대상이 되었다고 믿습니다."

raw: “Let us hope so,” said the uncle. “Detestation of the high is the involuntary homage of the low.”
en: "Let us hope so," said the uncle. "The hatred of the lower classes is the involuntary respect they pay to the high."
ko: "그러기를 바라자꾸나," 삼촌이 말했다. "하층 계급의 증오야말로 그들이 상류층에게 바치는 본의 아닌 존경인 것이다."

raw: “There is not,” pursued the nephew, in his former tone, “a face I can look at, in all this country round about us, which looks at me with any deference on it but the dark deference of fear and slavery.”
en: The nephew continued, "There is not a single face in this area that looks at me with respect. They only show the fear and submission of slaves."
ko: 조카가 계속했다, "이 지역에서 저를 존경심으로 바라보는 얼굴은 단 하나도 없습니다. 그들은 오직 노예의 두려움과 복종만을 보여줄 뿐입니다."

raw: “A compliment,” said the Marquis, “to the grandeur of the family, merited by the manner in which the family has sustained its grandeur.
en: The Marquis said, "A compliment to the family's power, which we have maintained well.
ko: 후작이 말했다, "우리가 잘 유지해 온 가문의 권력에 대한 찬사로구나.

raw: Hah!” And he took another gentle little pinch of snuff, and lightly crossed his legs.
en: Ah!" He took another pinch of snuff and crossed his legs.
ko: 아!" 그는 코담배를 한 줌 더 쥐고 다리를 꼬았다.

raw: But, when his nephew, leaning an elbow on the table, covered his eyes thoughtfully and dejectedly with his hand, the fine mask looked at him sideways with a stronger concentration of keenness, closeness, and dislike, than was comportable with its wearer’s assumption of indifference.
en: But when his nephew leaned on the table and covered his eyes in depression, the Marquis looked at him sideways with sharp dislike, dropping his mask of indifference.
ko: 하지만 그의 조카가 우울해하며 탁자에 기대어 눈을 가리자, 후작은 무관심의 가면을 벗어던지고 강한 반감을 드러내며 그를 곁눈질했다.

raw: “Repression is the only lasting philosophy.
en: "Repression is the only philosophy that lasts," the Marquis remarked.
ko: "억압만이 지속되는 유일한 철학이다," 후작이 말했다.

raw: The dark deference of fear and slavery, my friend,” observed the Marquis, “will keep the dogs obedient to the whip, as long as this roof,” looking up to it, “shuts out the sky.”
en: He glanced upward. "The fear and submission of slaves, my friend, will keep these dogs obedient to the whip, as long as this roof stands."
ko: 그가 위를 힐끗 보았다. "노예의 두려움과 복종이, 내 친구여, 이 지붕이 서 있는 한 이 개들이 채찍에 복종하도록 만들 것이다."

raw: That might not be so long as the Marquis supposed.
en: That might not be as long as the Marquis thought.
ko: 그것은 후작이 생각한 것만큼 길지 않을지도 모른다.

raw: If a picture of the chateau as it was to be a very few years hence, and of fifty like it as they too were to be a very few years hence, could have been shown to him that night, he might have been at a loss to claim his own from the ghastly, fire-charred, plunder-wrecked rains.
en: If he could have been shown a picture of the castle as it would be in just a few years, and of fifty others like it, he might not have even recognized his own home among the horrifying, fire-scorched, and looted ruins.
ko: 만약 불과 몇 년 후에 성이 어떤 모습이 될지, 그리고 그와 같은 오십 개의 다른 성들이 어떻게 될지를 보여주는 그림이 그에게 주어졌다면, 그는 끔찍하고 불에 타고 약탈당한 폐허 속에서 자기 집조차 알아보지 못했을지도 모른다.

raw: As for the roof he vaunted, he might have found _that_ shutting out the sky in a new way--to wit, for ever, from the eyes of the bodies into which its lead was fired, out of the barrels of a hundred thousand muskets.
en: As for the roof he bragged about, it would shut out the sky forever for the men who would be shot by the lead melted from it.
ko: 그가 자랑하던 그 지붕에 대해 말하자면, 그것은 거기서 녹아내린 납으로 총에 맞을 사람들에게 영원히 하늘을 가려버릴 것이었다.

raw: “Meanwhile,” said the Marquis, “I will preserve the honour and repose of the family, if you will not.
en: The Marquis said, "Meanwhile, I will preserve the family honor and peace, even if you won't.
ko: 후작이 말했다, "그동안 나는 가문의 명예와 평화를 지키겠다. 네가 그렇지 않다 하더라도 말이다.

raw: But you must be fatigued.
en: But you must be tired.
ko: 하지만 너도 피곤하겠구나.

raw: Shall we terminate our conference for the night?”
en: Shall we end our talk for the night?"
ko: 오늘 밤 이야기는 이만 끝낼까?"

raw: “A moment more.”
en: "A moment more."
ko: "조금만 더요."

raw: “An hour, if you please.”
en: "An hour, if you like."
ko: "네가 원한다면 한 시간이라도."

raw: “Sir,” said the nephew, “we have done wrong, and are reaping the fruits of wrong.”
en: The nephew said, "Sir, we have done wrong, and we are paying the price."
ko: 조카가 말했다, "삼촌, 우리는 잘못을 저질렀고, 그 대가를 치르고 있습니다."

raw: “_We_ have done wrong?” repeated the Marquis, with an inquiring smile, and delicately pointing, first to his nephew, then to himself.
en: "_We_ have done wrong?" the Marquis repeated with a smile, pointing to his nephew and himself.
ko: "_우리가_ 잘못을 저질렀다고?" 후작은 미소를 지으며 조카와 자신을 가리키며 반복했다.

raw: “Our family; our honourable family, whose honour is of so much account to both of us, in such different ways.
en: "Our family; our honorable family, whose honor means so much to both of us, though in very different ways.
ko: "우리 가문 말입니다. 비록 매우 다른 방식이긴 하지만, 우리 두 사람 모두에게 그 명예가 너무나도 큰 의미를 지니는, 우리의 명예로운 가문 말입니다.

raw: Even in my father’s time, we did a world of wrong, injuring every human creature who came between us and our pleasure, whatever it was. Why need I speak of my father’s time, when it is equally yours?
en: Even in my father's time, we did terrible wrongs, injuring anyone who stood in the way of our pleasure.
ko: 제 아버지 시대에도 우리는 우리의 쾌락에 방해가 되는 사람이라면 누구든 해치며 끔찍한 잘못을 저질렀습니다.

raw: Can I separate my father’s twin-brother, joint inheritor, and next successor, from himself?”
en: I cannot separate my father from his twin brother, his partner and successor."
ko: 저는 제 아버지를 그의 쌍둥이 형제이자 파트너이며 후계자인 분과 분리해서 생각할 수 없습니다."

raw: “Death has done that!” said the Marquis.
en: "Death has done that!" said the Marquis.
ko: "죽음이 그렇게 했지!" 후작이 말했다.

raw: “And has left me,” answered the nephew, “bound to a system that is frightful to me, responsible for it, but powerless in it; seeking to execute the last request of my dear mother’s lips, and obey the last look of my dear mother’s eyes, which implored me to have mercy and to redress; and tortured by seeking assistance and power in vain.”
en: The nephew answered, "And left me tied to a system I hate, responsible for it but powerless to change it. I am trying to carry out my mother's last request to show mercy and correct our wrongs, but I am powerless."
ko: 조카는 대답했다, "그리고 제가 증오하는 시스템에 저를 묶어 두셨고, 그 시스템에 대한 책임은 있지만 바꿀 힘은 없게 만드셨죠. 저는 자비를 베풀고 우리의 잘못을 바로잡으라는 어머니의 마지막 부탁을 실천하려 노력하고 있지만, 무력할 뿐입니다."

raw: “Seeking them from me, my nephew,” said the Marquis, touching him on the breast with his forefinger--they were now standing by the hearth--“you will for ever seek them in vain, be assured.”
en: "You will never find help or power from me, my nephew," said the Marquis, touching him on the chest with his finger as they stood by the fire.
ko: "내게서는 어떤 도움이나 힘도 얻지 못할 거다, 내 조카야," 후작이 난롯가에 서서 손가락으로 그의 가슴을 찌르며 말했다.

raw: Every fine straight line in the clear whiteness of his face, was cruelly, craftily, and closely compressed, while he stood looking quietly at his nephew, with his snuff-box in his hand.
en: Every line on his pale face was tightened in a cruel, sharp expression as he looked at his nephew, holding his snuffbox.
ko: 그가 코담배 갑을 든 채 조카를 바라보았을 때, 그의 창백한 얼굴의 모든 선은 잔인하고 날카로운 표정으로 굳어졌다.

raw: Once again he touched him on the breast, as though his finger were the fine point of a small sword, with which, in delicate finesse, he ran him through the body, and said,
en: He touched him on the chest again, as if his finger were a sword running him through, and said:
ko: 그는 마치 자기 손가락이 그를 관통하는 검인 것처럼 그의 가슴을 다시 찌르며 말했다:

raw: “My friend, I will die, perpetuating the system under which I have lived.”
en: "My friend, I will die supporting the system under which I have lived."
ko: "내 친구여, 나는 내가 살아온 시스템을 지지하다가 죽을 것이다."

raw: When he had said it, he took a culminating pinch of snuff, and put his box in his pocket.
en: Having said this, he took a pinch of snuff and put the box in his pocket.
ko: 이 말을 한 후, 그는 코담배를 한 줌 집어 들고 상자를 주머니에 넣었다.

raw: “Better to be a rational creature,” he added then, after ringing a small bell on the table, “and accept your natural destiny.
en: "It is better to be sensible," he added, ringing a bell, "and accept your destiny.
ko: "현명해지는 게 좋을 거다," 그는 종을 울리며 덧붙였다, "그리고 네 운명을 받아들여라.

raw: But you are lost, Monsieur Charles, I see.”
en: But you are lost, Charles, I see."
ko: 하지만 너는 길을 잃었구나, 찰스. 내 눈엔 보인다."

raw: “This property and France are lost to me,” said the nephew, sadly; “I renounce them.”
en: "This property and France are lost to me," said the nephew sadly. "I give them up."
ko: "이 재산과 프랑스는 제게서 사라졌습니다," 조카가 슬프게 말했다. "저는 그것들을 포기합니다."

raw: “Are they both yours to renounce?
en: "Are they yours to give up?
ko: "네가 포기할 수 있는 너의 것이기나 하느냐?

raw: France may be, but is the property?
en: France might be, but is the property?
ko: 프랑스는 그럴지 모르겠지만, 이 재산은?

raw: It is scarcely worth mentioning; but, is it yet?”
en: It is hardly worth mentioning, but is it yours yet?"
ko: 언급할 가치도 없지만, 그것이 이미 네 것이냐?"

raw: “I had no intention, in the words I used, to claim it yet.
en: "I did not mean to claim it yet.
ko: "아직 제 것이라고 주장하려는 뜻은 아니었습니다.

raw: If it passed to me from you, to-morrow--”
en: If it passed to me tomorrow, "
ko: 만약 내일 그것이 제게 넘어온다 해도, "

raw: “Which I have the vanity to hope is not probable.”
en: "Which I hope is not likely."
ko: "그럴 일은 없길 바란다만."

raw: “--or twenty years hence--” “You do me too much honour,” said the Marquis; “still, I prefer that supposition.” “--I would abandon it, and live otherwise and elsewhere.
en:
"—or twenty years from now—"
"You do me too much honor," said the Marquis; "still, I prefer that guess."
"—I would abandon it, and live differently and elsewhere.
ko:
“—아니면 이십 년 후일 수도 있지요—”
“나를 너무 높이 평가하는군.” 후작이 말했다. “그래도 난 그 추측이 더 마음에 드네.”
“—저는 그것을 버리고 다른 곳에서 다른 방식으로 살겠습니다.”

raw: It is little to relinquish.
en: It is little to give up.
ko: 포기하기엔 보잘것없는 것이죠.

raw: What is it but a wilderness of misery and ruin!”
en: It is just a wilderness of misery and ruin!"
ko: 이곳은 그저 비참함과 파멸의 황무지일 뿐입니다!"

raw: “Hah!” said the Marquis, glancing round the luxurious room.
en: "Ah!" said the Marquis, looking around the luxurious room.
ko: "아!" 후작이 호화로운 방을 둘러보며 말했다.

raw: “To the eye it is fair enough, here; but seen in its integrity, under the sky, and by the daylight, it is a crumbling tower of waste, mismanagement, extortion, debt, mortgage, oppression, hunger, nakedness, and suffering.”
en: "It looks beautiful here," the nephew said. "But in reality, it is a crumbling tower. Waste, debt, oppression, hunger, and suffering, that is what it is made of."
ko: "여기는 아름다워 보입니다," 조카가 말했다. "하지만 현실에서, 이곳은 무너져 내리는 탑입니다. 낭비, 빚, 억압, 굶주림, 그리고 고통, 그것이 바로 이것을 이루고 있는 것들입니다."

raw: “Hah!” said the Marquis again, in a well-satisfied manner.
en: "Ah!" the Marquis said again, looking very satisfied.
ko: "아!" 후작이 매우 만족스러운 표정으로 다시 말했다.

raw: “If it ever becomes mine, it shall be put into some hands better qualified to free it slowly (if such a thing is possible) from the weight that drags it down, so that the miserable people who cannot leave it and who have been long wrung to the last point of endurance, may, in another generation, suffer less; but it is not for me.
en: "If it ever becomes mine, I will put it into hands that can slowly free it from this debt, so the poor people who cannot leave can suffer less in the next generation. But it is not for me.
ko: "만약 이것이 제 것이 된다면, 저는 서서히 이 빚에서 벗어날 수 있게 해 줄 사람들의 손에 맡기겠습니다. 그래서 떠날 수 없는 가난한 사람들이 다음 세대에서는 덜 고통받을 수 있게요. 하지만 이것은 저를 위한 것이 아닙니다.

raw: There is a curse on it, and on all this land.”
en: There is a curse on this land."
ko: 이 땅에는 저주가 내려져 있습니다."

raw: “And you?” said the uncle. “Forgive my curiosity; do you, under your new philosophy, graciously intend to live?”
en: "And you?" the uncle asked. "Forgive my curiosity, but how do you plan to live?"
ko: "그리고 너는?" 삼촌이 물었다. "내 호기심을 용서하거라, 하지만 넌 어떻게 살 계획이냐?"

raw: “I must do, to live, what others of my countrymen, even with nobility at their backs, may have to do some day--work.”
en: "I must do what other noblemen may have to do one day, work."
ko: "다른 귀족들도 언젠가 해야 할지도 모르는 일, 즉 일을 해야 합니다."

raw: “In England, for example?”
en: "In England, for example?"
ko: "예를 들면, 영국에서 말이냐?"

raw: “Yes.
en: "Yes.

raw: The family honour, sir, is safe from me in this country. The family name can suffer from me in no other, for I bear it in no other.”
en: The family name will be safe from me there, because I do not use it."
ko: 가문의 이름은 제가 그곳에서 사용하지 않기 때문에 안전할 것입니다."

raw: The ringing of the bell had caused the adjoining bed-chamber to be lighted. It now shone brightly, through the door of communication.
en: The ringing of the bell had summoned the servant to light the bedroom next door, which now shone through the open entrance.
ko: 종소리가 하인을 불러 옆 침실에 불을 밝히게 했고, 그 빛이 열린 문을 통해 비쳐나왔다.

raw: The Marquis looked that way, and listened for the retreating step of his valet.
en: The Marquis looked that way, listening for his servant's footsteps.
ko: 후작은 하인의 발소리에 귀를 기울이며 그쪽을 바라보았다.

raw: “England is very attractive to you, seeing how indifferently you have prospered there,” he observed then, turning his calm face to his nephew with a smile.
en: "England is very attractive to you, considering how poorly you have done there," he remarked with a smile.
ko: "네가 그곳에서 얼마나 형편없이 지냈는지를 생각하면 영국은 네게 매우 매력적이구나." 그가 미소를 지으며 말했다.

raw: “I have already said, that for my prospering there, I am sensible I may be indebted to you, sir.
en: "I have already said that my difficulties there may be due to you, sir.
ko: "제가 그곳에서 겪는 어려움은 삼촌 때문일 수도 있다고 이미 말씀드렸습니다.

raw: For the rest, it is my Refuge.”
en: For the rest, it is my refuge."
ko: 그 외의 것에 관해서라면, 그곳은 제 피난처입니다."

raw: “They say, those boastful English, that it is the Refuge of many.
en: "The English boast that their country is a refuge for many.
ko: "영국인들은 자기네 나라가 많은 이들에게 피난처라고 자랑하지.

raw: You know a compatriot who has found a Refuge there?
en: Do you know a fellow countryman who has found refuge there?
ko: 그곳으로 피신한 동향 사람을 알고 있느냐?

raw: A Doctor?”
en: A Doctor?"
ko: 의사 말이다."

raw: “Yes.”
en: "Yes."
ko: "알고 있습니다."

raw: “With a daughter?”
en: "With a daughter?"
ko: "딸이 있는?"

raw: “Yes.”
en: "Yes."

raw: “Yes,” said the Marquis. “You are fatigued.
en: "Yes," said the Marquis. "You are tired.
ko: "그렇군," 후작이 말했다. "피곤하겠구나.

raw: Good night!”
en: Good night!"
ko: 잘 자거라!"

raw: As he bent his head in his most courtly manner, there was a secrecy in his smiling face, and he conveyed an air of mystery to those words, which struck the eyes and ears of his nephew forcibly.
en: He bowed politely, but there was a secret, mocking look on his face as he spoke those words, which startled his nephew.
ko: 그는 정중하게 고개를 숙였지만, 그 말을 할 때 얼굴에는 은밀하고 조롱하는 듯한 표정이 있었고, 그것이 조카를 깜짝 놀라게 했다.

raw: At the same time, the thin straight lines of the setting of the eyes, and the thin straight lips, and the markings in the nose, curved with a sarcasm that looked handsomely diabolic.
en: At the same time, the thin, straight lines around his eyes, his thin, straight lips, and the features of his nose curved into a sarcastic smile that looked handsomely devilish.
ko: 동시에 그의 눈가의 얇고 곧은 주름과 얇고 일자형인 입술, 그리고 코의 윤곽이 비꼬는 듯한 미소로 휘어지며 잘생긴 악마처럼 보였다.

raw: “Yes,” repeated the Marquis. “A Doctor with a daughter.
en: "Yes," the Marquis repeated. "A Doctor with a daughter.
ko: "그렇지," 후작이 반복했다. "딸이 있는 의사.

raw: Yes.
en: Yes.
ko: 그래.

raw: So commences the new philosophy!
en: So begins your new philosophy!
ko: 그렇게 너의 새로운 철학이 시작되는구나!

raw: You are fatigued.
en: You are tired.
ko: 피곤할 테지.

raw: Good night!”
en: Good night!"
ko: 잘 자거라!"

raw: It would have been of as much avail to interrogate any stone face outside the chateau as to interrogate that face of his.
en: It would have been just as useful to question any stone face outside the castle as it would be to question his face.
ko: 그의 얼굴에 질문을 던지는 것은 성 밖의 돌 얼굴에 질문을 던지는 것만큼이나 소용없는 일이었다.

raw: The nephew looked at him, in vain, in passing on to the door.
en: The nephew looked at him in vain as he walked to the door.
ko: 조카가 문 쪽으로 걸어가는 그를 헛되이 쳐다보았다.

raw: “Good night!” said the uncle. “I look to the pleasure of seeing you again in the morning.
en: "Good night!" said the uncle. "I look forward to seeing you in the morning.
ko: "잘 자거라!" 삼촌이 말했다. "아침에 만나길 기대하마.

raw: Good repose!
en: Rest well!
ko: 푹 쉬거라!

raw: Light Monsieur my nephew to his chamber there!--And burn Monsieur my nephew in his bed, if you will,” he added to himself, before he rang his little bell again, and summoned his valet to his own bedroom.
en: Show my nephew to his room, and burn him in his bed if you like," he added to himself, before summoning his servant to his own room.
ko: 내 조카를 방으로 안내하고, 원한다면 침대에서 그를 불태워버려라," 그는 속으로 덧붙이고는 자신의 하인을 자기 방으로 불렀다.

raw: The valet come and gone, Monsieur the Marquis walked to and fro in his loose chamber-robe, to prepare himself gently for sleep, that hot still night.
en: Once the servant left, the Marquis walked around his bedroom in his robe, getting ready for bed on this hot night.
ko: 하인이 떠나자, 후작은 이 무더운 밤 잠자리에 들 준비를 하며 가운 차림으로 침실을 서성였다.

raw: Rustling about the room, his softly-slippered feet making no noise on the floor, he moved like a refined tiger:--looked like some enchanted marquis of the impenitently wicked sort, in story, whose periodical change into tiger form was either just going off, or just coming on.
en: Moving quietly in his slippers, he looked like a tiger, or an enchanted marquis from a fairy tale who was about to turn into a beast.
ko: 슬리퍼를 신고 조용히 움직이는 그는 마치 호랑이 같기도 했고, 짐승으로 변하기 직전의 동화 속 마법에 걸린 후작 같기도 했다.

raw: He moved from end to end of his voluptuous bedroom, looking again at the scraps of the day’s journey that came unbidden into his mind; the slow toil up the hill at sunset, the setting sun, the descent, the mill, the prison on the crag, the little village in the hollow, the peasants at the fountain, and the mender of roads with his blue cap pointing out the chain under the carriage.
en: He walked around the luxurious room, thinking of the day's journey. He saw it in pieces: the slow climb up the hill, the sunset, the mill, the prison on the cliff. Then the poor village. The peasants by the fountain. And the road mender pointing out the man under the carriage.
ko: 그는 그날의 여정을 생각하며 호화로운 방 안을 돌아다녔다. 천천히 언덕을 오르던 일, 일몰, 방앗간, 절벽 위의 감옥 등 조각조각 난 장면들이 떠올랐다. 그리고 가난한 마을. 분수대 옆의 농부들. 마차 밑의 남자를 가리키던 도로 수리공도.

raw: That fountain suggested the Paris fountain, the little bundle lying on the step, the women bending over it, and the tall man with his arms up, crying, “Dead!”
en: That fountain reminded him of the one in Paris, the dead child, the crying father, and the women looking at the body.
ko: 그 분수대는 그에게 파리의 분수대, 죽은 아이, 울부짖는 아버지, 그리고 시신을 바라보던 여성들을 떠올리게 했다.

raw: “I am cool now,” said Monsieur the Marquis, “and may go to bed.”
en: The Marquis said, "I am cool now, and can go to bed."
ko: 후작은 말했다, "이제 열기가 좀 식었으니 자러 가야겠다."

raw: So, leaving only one light burning on the large hearth, he let his thin gauze curtains fall around him, and heard the night break its silence with a long sigh as he composed himself to sleep.
en: Leaving only one light burning, he let his gauze curtains fall around his bed and went to sleep as the night fell silent.
ko: 그는 불 하나만 켜 둔 채 침대 주위로 얇은 커튼을 내리고 밤이 깊어 고요해지자 잠이 들었다.

raw: The stone faces on the outer walls stared blindly at the black night for three heavy hours; for three heavy hours, the horses in the stables rattled at their racks, the dogs barked, and the owl made a noise with very little resemblance in it to the noise conventionally assigned to the owl by men-poets.
en: The stone faces on the outer walls stared blindly into the black night for three long hours; for three long hours, the horses in the stables rattled at their feeding racks, the dogs barked, and the owl made a noise that sounded very little like the noise poets usually imagine owls make.
ko: 외벽의 돌 얼굴들은 길고 긴 세 시간 동안 맹목적으로 칠흑 같은 밤을 응시했다. 길고 긴 세 시간 동안, 마구간의 말들은 여물통을 덜그럭거렸고, 개들은 짖었으며, 올빼미는 시인들이 흔히 상상하는 올빼미 소리와는 전혀 다른 소리를 냈다.

raw: But it is the obstinate custom of such creatures hardly ever to say what is set down for them.
en: In the stables, the horses rattled their chains, the dogs barked, and the owl hooted.
ko: 마구간에서는 말들이 쇠사슬을 덜그럭거렸고, 개들은 짖었으며, 올빼미는 부엉거렸다.

raw: For three heavy hours, the stone faces of the chateau, lion and human, stared blindly at the night. Dead darkness lay on all the landscape, dead darkness added its own hush to the hushing dust on all the roads.
en: For three heavy hours, the stone faces of the castle, both lion and human, stared blindly into the night. A dead darkness lay over the entire landscape, adding its own silence to the quiet dust on all the roads.
ko: 세 시간이라는 무거운 시간 동안, 사자와 사람의 모습을 한 성의 돌 얼굴들은 맹목적으로 밤을 노려보았다. 죽은 듯한 어둠이 전체 풍경 위에 내려앉아 모든 도로의 조용한 먼지에 침묵을 더했다.

raw: The burial-place had got to the pass that its little heaps of poor grass were undistinguishable from one another; the figure on the Cross might have come down, for anything that could be seen of it.
en: The cemetery was so dark that its little heaps of poor grass could not be told apart; the figure of Jesus on the Cross might have come down, for all that could be seen of it in the gloom.
ko: 공동묘지는 너무 어두워서 형편없는 풀무더기들조차 분간할 수 없었다. 그 어둠 속에서 보이는 것이라곤 십자가에 못 박힌 예수상이 내려왔을지도 모른다는 것뿐이었다.

raw: In the village, taxers and taxed were fast asleep. Dreaming, perhaps, of banquets, as the starved usually do, and of ease and rest, as the driven slave and the yoked ox may, its lean inhabitants slept soundly, and were fed and freed.
en: In the village, both the tax collectors and the poor peasants were fast asleep, dreaming of food and rest as yoked oxen do.
ko: 마을에서는 세금 징수원과 가난한 농부들 모두 깊은 잠에 빠져, 멍에를 멘 소들처럼 음식과 휴식을 꿈꾸고 있었다.

raw: The fountain in the village flowed unseen and unheard, and the fountain at the chateau dropped unseen and unheard--both melting away, like the minutes that were falling from the spring of Time--through three dark hours.
en: The village fountain flowed unseen in the dark, and the castle fountain splashed quietly, both counting the minutes of the three dark hours.
ko: 마을의 분수는 어둠 속에서 보이지 않게 흘렀고, 성의 분수는 조용히 물을 튀기며 세 시간이라는 어두운 시간의 분을 세고 있었다.

raw: Then, the grey water of both began to be ghostly in the light, and the eyes of the stone faces of the chateau were opened.
en: Then, the water began to look gray in the dawn light, and the stone faces on the castle seemed to open their eyes.
ko: 그러다 새벽빛에 물이 잿빛으로 보이기 시작했고, 성벽의 돌 얼굴들이 눈을 뜨는 것 같았다.

raw: Lighter and lighter, until at last the sun touched the tops of the still trees, and poured its radiance over the hill.
en: The light grew stronger until the sun touched the trees and shone over the hill.
ko: 빛이 점점 강해지더니 마침내 태양이 나무들에 닿고 언덕 위로 빛났다.

raw: In the glow, the water of the chateau fountain seemed to turn to blood, and the stone faces crimsoned.
en: In the red light, the castle fountain water looked like blood, and the stone faces turned red.
ko: 붉은 빛 속에서 성의 분숫물은 피처럼 보였고, 돌 얼굴들도 붉게 변했다.

raw: The carol of the birds was loud and high, and, on the weather-beaten sill of the great window of the bed-chamber of Monsieur the Marquis, one little bird sang its sweetest song with all its might.
en: The singing of the birds was loud and high, and on the weathered sill of the large window of the Marquis's bedroom, one little bird sang its sweetest song with all its might.
ko: 새들의 노랫소리는 크고 높았으며, 후작의 침실에 있는 커다란 창문의 풍화된 창틀 위에서는 작은 새 한 마리가 온 힘을 다해 가장 달콤한 노래를 부르고 있었다.

raw: At this, the nearest stone face seemed to stare amazed, and, with open mouth and dropped under-jaw, looked awe-stricken.
en: The nearest stone face seemed to stare in shock, with its mouth open.
ko: 가장 가까운 돌 얼굴은 입을 벌린 채 충격에 빠져 응시하는 듯했다.

raw: Now, the sun was full up, and movement began in the village.
en: With the sun up, the village awoke.
ko: 해가 뜨자 마을이 깨어났다.

raw: Casement windows opened, crazy doors were unbarred, and people came forth shivering--chilled, as yet, by the new sweet air.
en: Windows were opened, doors unlocked, and people walked out shivering in the morning air.
ko: 창문이 열리고 문이 잠금 해제되었으며, 사람들은 아침 공기에 몸을 떨며 걸어 나왔다.

raw: Then began the rarely lightened toil of the day among the village population.
en: Then the endless, heavy daily work began among the village people.
ko: 그리고 마을 사람들 사이에서 끝없고 고된 일상 업무가 시작되었다.

raw: Some, to the fountain; some, to the fields; men and women here, to dig and delve; men and women there, to see to the poor live stock, and lead the bony cows out, to such pasture as could be found by the roadside.
en: Some went to the fountain, some to the fields to dig, and some led their thin cows to find grass by the roadside.
ko: 어떤 이들은 분수대로 갔고, 어떤 이들은 땅을 파러 들판으로 나갔으며, 또 어떤 이들은 길가에서 풀을 찾기 위해 마른 소들을 끌고 갔다.

raw: In the church and at the Cross, a kneeling figure or two; attendant on the latter prayers, the led cow, trying for a breakfast among the weeds at its foot.
en: In the church and at the Cross, a kneeling figure or two could be seen; next to the people praying at the Cross, a tethered cow tried to find breakfast among the weeds at its base.
ko: 교회와 십자가에서는 무릎을 꿇은 한두 명의 사람들을 볼 수 있었고, 십자가에서 기도하는 사람들 옆에서는 묶인 소 한 마리가 그 밑동의 잡초 사이에서 아침 식사를 찾으려 애쓰고 있었다.

raw: The chateau awoke later, as became its quality, but awoke gradually and surely.
en: The castle awoke later, as suited its high status, but it awoke gradually and surely.
ko: 성은 그 높은 신분에 걸맞게 늦게 깨어났지만, 점진적이면서도 확실하게 깨어났다.

raw: First, the lonely boar-spears and knives of the chase had been reddened as of old; then, had gleamed trenchant in the morning sunshine; now, doors and windows were thrown open, horses in their stables looked round over their shoulders at the light and freshness pouring in at doorways, leaves sparkled and rustled at iron-grated windows, dogs pulled hard at their chains, and reared impatient to be loosed.
en: First, the morning sun shone red on the boar spears and hunting knives, just as it had in the old days; then, doors and windows were thrown open, horses in their stables looked back over their shoulders at the light and fresh air pouring in, leaves sparkled and rustled at iron-grated windows, and dogs pulled hard at their chains, jumping impatiently to be let loose.
ko: 먼저, 옛날과 다름없이 아침 해가 멧돼지 창과 사냥용 칼 위로 붉게 비췄다. 그런 다음 문과 창문이 활짝 열렸고, 마구간의 말들은 쏟아져 들어오는 빛과 신선한 공기를 어깨 너머로 돌아보았으며, 쇠창살 창문에서는 나뭇잎이 반짝이며 바스락거렸고, 개들은 사슬을 세게 당기며 풀려나기를 초조하게 기다리며 펄쩍펄쩍 뛰었다.

raw: All these trivial incidents belonged to the routine of life, and the return of morning.
en: All these small events belonged to the normal routine of life and the return of morning.
ko: 이 모든 작은 사건들은 삶의 평범한 일상과 아침의 귀환에 속하는 것들이었다.

raw: Surely, not so the ringing of the great bell of the chateau, nor the running up and down the stairs; nor the hurried figures on the terrace; nor the booting and tramping here and there and everywhere, nor the quick saddling of horses and riding away?
en: But the sudden ringing of the great castle bell, the sound of people running up and down the stairs, and the panic on the terrace were not normal. Servants saddled horses and rode away in a hurry.
ko: 그러나 성의 큰 종이 갑자기 울리고, 사람들이 계단을 오르내리는 소리와 테라스에서의 혼란은 정상이 아니었다. 하인들은 말에 안장을 얹고 서둘러 타고 떠났다.

raw: What winds conveyed this hurry to the grizzled mender of roads, already at work on the hill-top beyond the village, with his day’s dinner (not much to carry) lying in a bundle that it was worth no crow’s while to peck at, on a heap of stones?
en: What invisible winds carried this sense of panic to the gray-haired road mender? He was already at work on the hilltop beyond the village, with his day's dinner—which wasn't much to carry—lying in a bundle on a pile of stones, so meager that it wasn't even worth a crow's time to peck at.
ko: 어떤 보이지 않는 바람이 이 공포감을 백발의 도로 수리공에게 실어 날랐을까? 그는 이미 마을 너머 언덕 꼭대기에서 일하고 있었고, 들고 다닐 것도 별로 없는 하루 치 저녁 식사는 돌무더기 위 보따리 속에 놓여 있었는데, 까마귀가 쪼아먹을 시간조차 아까울 정도로 빈약했다.

raw: Had the birds, carrying some grains of it to a distance, dropped one over him as they sow chance seeds? Whether or no, the mender of roads ran, on the sultry morning, as if for his life, down the hill, knee-high in dust, and never stopped till he got to the fountain.
en: Did the birds, carrying some grains of the news to a distance, drop one on him like they drop random seeds? Whether they did or not, the road mender ran on that hot morning as if running for his life, down the hill through knee-high dust, and he never stopped until he reached the village fountain.
ko: 멀리 소식의 알갱이들을 실어 나르던 새들이 무작위로 씨앗을 떨어뜨리듯 그에게 하나를 떨어뜨렸을까? 그들이 그랬든 아니든, 도로 수리공은 그 더운 아침에 마치 목숨을 걸고 달리는 것처럼 무릎 높이의 먼지를 헤치고 언덕을 뛰어내려 갔으며, 마을 분수대에 도달할 때까지 결코 멈추지 않았다.

raw: All the people of the village were at the fountain, standing about in their depressed manner, and whispering low, but showing no other emotions than grim curiosity and surprise.
en: All the village people were gathered at the fountain, standing around in their usual depressed manner and whispering quietly, showing no emotions other than grim curiosity and surprise.
ko: 마을 사람들은 모두 분수대에 모여 평소처럼 우울한 태도로 서서 조용히 속삭이고 있었으며, 암울한 호기심과 놀라움 외에는 아무런 감정도 보이지 않았다.

raw: The led cows, hastily brought in and tethered to anything that would hold them, were looking stupidly on, or lying down chewing the cud of nothing particularly repaying their trouble, which they had picked up in their interrupted saunter.
en: The tethered cows, hastily brought in and tied to anything that would hold them, were looking on stupidly, or lying down chewing whatever unrewarding cud they had picked up during their interrupted morning walk.
ko: 서둘러 끌려와 묶일 만한 곳이면 어디든 묶인 소들은 멍청하게 쳐다보거나 엎드려 방해받은 아침 산책 중에 주워 먹은 보잘것없는 먹이를 되새김질하고 있었다.

raw: Some of the people of the chateau, and some of those of the posting-house, and all the taxing authorities, were armed more or less, and were crowded on the other side of the little street in a purposeless way, that was highly fraught with nothing.
en: Some of the castle servants, some people from the inn, and all the tax officials were more or less armed, crowding aimlessly on the other side of the little street in a confused way that suggested they had no real plan.
ko: 일부 성의 하인들과 여관 사람들, 그리고 모든 세무 관리들은 다소 무장한 채 좁은 거리 반대편에 목적 없이 모여 있었는데, 그들의 혼란스러운 모습은 아무런 실질적인 계획이 없음을 보여주었다.

raw: Already, the mender of roads had penetrated into the midst of a group of fifty particular friends, and was smiting himself in the breast with his blue cap. What did all this portend, and what portended the swift hoisting-up of Monsieur Gabelle behind a servant on horseback, and the conveying away of the said Gabelle (double-laden though the horse was), at a gallop, like a new version of the German ballad of Leonora?
en: Already, the road mender had pushed his way into the middle of a group of fifty specific friends, and he was beating himself on the chest with his blue cap. What did all this mean? And what was the meaning of Monsieur Gabelle being quickly hoisted up behind a servant on horseback, and ridden away at a gallop, even though the horse was carrying a double load, like a scene from an old German ballad?
ko: 이미 도로 수리공은 오십 명의 지인들 무리 한가운데로 밀고 들어가 파란 모자로 자신의 가슴을 치고 있었다. 이 모든 것이 무슨 의미일까? 그리고 말이 두 배의 짐을 지고 있음에도 불구하고 옛 독일 발라드의 한 장면처럼 가벨 씨가 말을 탄 하인 뒤에 재빨리 올라타 전속력으로 달려간 것은 무슨 의미였을까?

raw: It portended that there was one stone face too many, up at the chateau.
en: It meant there was one stone face too many at the castle.
ko: 그것은 성에 석상 얼굴이 하나 더 생겼다는 것을 의미했다.

raw: The Gorgon had surveyed the building again in the night, and had added the one stone face wanting; the stone face for which it had waited through about two hundred years.
en: The Gorgon had looked at the building during the night, adding the final stone face it had waited two hundred years for.
ko: 고르곤이 밤사이에 그 건물을 바라보며, 이백 년 동안 기다려온 마지막 석상 얼굴을 추가했던 것이다.

raw: It lay back on the pillow of Monsieur the Marquis.
en: It lay on the Marquis's pillow.
ko: 그것은 후작의 베개 위에 놓여 있었다.

raw: It was like a fine mask, suddenly startled, made angry, and petrified.
en: It looked like his mask-like face, but frozen in anger and petrified.
ko: 그것은 그의 가면 같은 얼굴처럼 보였지만, 분노로 얼어붙어 돌로 변해 있었다.

raw: Driven home into the heart of the stone figure attached to it, was a knife.
en: Driven deep into the stone figure's heart was a knife.
ko: 그 돌 형상의 심장 깊숙이 칼이 박혀 있었다.

raw: Round its hilt was a frill of paper, on which was scrawled:
en: Around the handle was a piece of paper, on which was written:
ko: 손잡이 주변에는 종이 한 장이 있었고, 거기에는 다음과 같이 쓰여 있었다:

raw: “Drive him fast to his tomb.
en: "Drive him fast to his tomb.
ko: "그를 그의 무덤으로 빨리 몰아라.

raw: This, from Jacques.”
en: This, from Jacques."
ko: 자크가 남김."
